change.title: pr-37038-flat
change.description: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: canManage() is granted by the VIEW scope
findings.body: `canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so an admin who was only given VIEW on all groups passes `requireManage()`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (GroupsResource.java:181) checks only `auth.groups().requireManage()`, which means a view-only group admin can create top-level groups and move groups to the top level. The per-group `canManage(group)` at line 79 correctly accepts only MANAGE. The fix is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Also update the javadoc at GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:75-76, which describes the same wrong rule, and add a negative test (VIEW on all groups, then creating a group returns 403).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs, not group IDs
findings.body:
Per-group resources are created with `name = groupId` and no type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-121). Only the all-groups resource gets `type = "Groups"` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:271-274). So `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` only ever visits the all-groups resource, and two things go wrong:
- `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` looks the resource up by name using its UUID (line 141), finds nothing, and falls back to the type resource.
- `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authz resource's UUID, not a group ID.

With an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission, `UsersResource.searchForUser` then sets `UserModel.GROUPS` to an ID that matches no group, and the JPA subquery (JpaUserProvider.java:762-765) filters out every user. The admin silently sees an empty user list. `getUsersCount` (UsersResource.java:398/425/430) gets the same wrong set. With per-group permissions only, the set is empty: no SQL filter is applied, and `first`/`max` are applied before the `canView` post-filter, so pages come back short. The V1 equivalent (GroupPermissions.java:313-316) maps the resource name back to the group ID. V2 should do the same with `resource.getName()`, and it needs a way to list the per-group resources (for example, set their type, or query policies on the Groups type). The new tests cover only per-group VIEW_MEMBERS, so they don't catch this.

findings.title: Group removal listener calls a method that V2 makes throw
findings.body: `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on (line 67-68). Its `groups()` now returns `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (GroupPermissionsV2.java:173-175). The listener is registered when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is on. Can both features be enabled at the same time? If they can, every group deletion would fail inside this listener.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers names the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but `requireManageMembers` is the counterpart of `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. Also, the `@return` at line 145 says "Stream", but the method returns a `Set`.

contracts.action: V2 group-level canManage() used by top-level group creation
contracts.equivalent_path: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(GroupModel) accepts only the MANAGE scope
contracts.before_after: Before this change, V2 used V1 GroupPermissions.canManage(), which required the manage-users role. Now an all-groups VIEW or MANAGE permission is enough.
contracts.visible_effect: A view-only admin can create top-level groups through POST /groups
contracts.failure_mode: Privilege escalation: VIEW grants a write action

contracts.action: User search filtered by the groups whose members the admin can view (V2)
contracts.equivalent_path: V1 GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission maps resource names back to group IDs
contracts.before_after: The removed filter(canView) was redundant, because toRepresentation still filters with canView. In V2, the group ID set contains resource UUIDs, or is empty.
contracts.visible_effect: Empty user list with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission; short pages otherwise
contracts.failure_mode: Wrong result with no error shown

summary: This PR adds a V2 Groups resource type for fine-grained admin permissions. It has one blocker: in V2, `canManage()` also accepts the VIEW scope, so an admin with only VIEW on all groups can create top-level groups. One fix: in V2, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` collects authz resource IDs instead of group IDs, which empties or skews user search and user counts without any error. Also included are a question about the group-removal listener (it may throw if V1 and V2 can both be enabled) and two javadoc mistakes. I didn't build or run any code.
